**What I found**
Billing should get its own module, `src/billing/index.js`, beside orders and shipping. Orders imports it, and billing imports nothing (the topology record calls this SPLIT). The change history decided it: all 24 finance rule commits in 26 weeks edited `src/orders/index.js`, none of them also carried an order ticket, and 3 of them broke order behaviour (ORD-82, ORD-85, ORD-88).

**Why it matters**
After the move, a tax, discount or invoice change edits only `src/billing/index.js`. That file never checks, stores or changes the status of an order. Without the move, roughly one finance change in eight keeps risking an order regression, as the record shows. The move is cheap to undo: one team, one caller, no data migration and one deployable.

```js
// src/billing/index.js: pure, imports nothing
// Amounts are integer cents; rates are basis points (2100 = 21%).
const TAX_BP = { nl: 2100, de: 1900, fr: 2000 };
const DISCOUNT_TIERS = [
  { overCents: 50000, cutBp: 1000 },
  { overCents: 10000, cutBp: 500 },
];

export function invoiceFor(customer, lines) {
  if (!(customer.country in TAX_BP)) throw new Error(`no tax rate for country ${customer.country}`);
  const subtotal = lines.reduce((sum, line) => sum + line.priceCents * line.quantity, 0);
  const tier = DISCOUNT_TIERS.find((candidate) => subtotal > candidate.overCents);
  const discount = tier ? Math.round((subtotal * tier.cutBp) / 10000) : 0;
  const tax = Math.round(((subtotal - discount) * TAX_BP[customer.country]) / 10000);
  return {
    lines: lines.map((line) => ({ label: line.sku, amountCents: line.priceCents * line.quantity })),
    discountCents: discount,
    taxCents: tax,
    totalCents: subtotal - discount + tax,
  };
}

// src/orders/index.js: placeOrder becomes
import { invoiceFor } from "../billing/index.js";
export function placeOrder(customer, lines) {
  if (lines.length === 0) throw new Error("an order needs at least one line");
  return save({ customer, lines, status: "placed", invoice: invoiceFor(customer, lines) });
}
```

The empty-order check still runs before the country check, so the error you get when both apply is unchanged. Rejecting a country with no tax rate moves to billing because it came from a finance ticket (FIN-214).
